Convolution layer: 3 → K channels
Demo
Use ◀ / ▶ to walk through the layer, or drive the controls yourself.
Emphasis
Click anywhere on the Filter Bank box to pick one filter of the bank. Drag the figure to orbit — the oblique shear eases out so you can see the true slabs; press “Figure view” to return to the printed pose.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-row block diagram of one convolutional layer, built from two perspective slab tensors with a labeled box between them. At the left a thin white slab is drawn as three stacked sheets seen nearly edge-on; the number 3 sits beneath it, 128 annotates its vertical left edge, 128 annotates the receding top edge, and the header above reads x_in in R, of shape 3 x 128 x 128. A hollow outlined block arrow points rightward into a rounded rectangle whose two lines of text read Filter Bank with 3x3 filters. A second hollow arrow leads to the right-hand slab, drawn in the same style but far thicker, with sets of three dots among its sheets marking omitted layers; 96 labels its depth, 128 its right vertical edge and 128 its lower receding edge, and the header reads x_out in R, of shape 96 x 128 x 128. Rendering both tensors identically reduces the comparison to thickness alone: the spatial dimensions stay at 128 by 128 while the channel count grows from 3 to 96. The layout supports working out, with concrete numbers, how many parameters each filter holds and how many filters the bank contains.

elements: Input tensor slab x_in drawn as 3 identical thin sheets stacked along a depth diagonal receding up-and-right, front-left face a true 128x128 square
Thin vertical separating lines on the input slab's top receding face marking the 3 channel sheets
Label '3' centered beneath the input slab (channel count)
Label '128' along the input slab's left vertical edge (height)
Label '128' along the input slab's upper receding edge (width/depth of the image plane)
Header text above the input slab: x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}
Hollow outlined block arrow (pentagon-shaped, white fill, black outline) pointing right from input slab to filter box
Rounded rectangle box with thick black outline and white fill, centered between the arrows
Two-line text inside the box: 'Filter Bank with' / '3x3 filters'
Second identical hollow outlined block arrow pointing right from the box to the output slab
Output tensor slab x_out drawn in the same style, far thicker, with many parallel sheet-separating lines
Two sets of three dots ('...') among the output slab sheets — one on the upper receding face, one on the front face — marking omitted channels
Label '96' centered beneath the output slab (channel count)
Label '128' along the output slab's right vertical edge
Label '128' along the output slab's lower receding edge
Header text above the output slab: x_out ∈ R^{96×128×128}
Hidden-until-clicked overlay inside the filter box: a 3×3×3 stack of small weight cells representing one selected filter
Highlight outline linking the selected filter's three 3×3 kernel slices to the three input channel sheets and to one output sheet

interactions.teaches: One filter spans ALL input channels: clicking a filter in the bank lights up its 3 kernel slices (27 weights = 3×3×3), all three input channel sheets it reads from, and the single output sheet it writes to — so each filter costs 3·3·3 = 27 parameters and produces exactly one output channel.

interactions.label: Number of filters in bank
interactions.teaches: The output slab's thickness and its channel label track the filter count one-for-one: K filters ⇒ K output channels, while the 128×128 face never changes.

interactions.label: Emphasis
interactions.teaches: Channel view shades the slab depth and the 3 → K sheet counts; spatial view shades the 128×128 faces instead, making visible that the layer changes only the channel dimension and preserves spatial resolution.
Rotating slightly off the oblique pose confirms the slabs are genuine 3D volumes — thin (3 sheets) versus thick (96 sheets) — rather than flat rectangles.

demo_steps.title: The input tensor
demo_steps.narration: Three channel sheets, each a 128×128 image plane, stacked into a thin slab: x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}.

demo_steps.title: One filter, 27 weights
demo_steps.narration: Click a filter in the bank: its three 3×3 kernel slices highlight along with all three input channels. Each filter holds 3×3×3 = 27 parameters and yields one output channel.

demo_steps.title: Growing the bank to 96 filters
demo_steps.narration: Drag the filter count up; the output slab thickens and its label climbs from 3 toward 96. Filter count is output channel count — 96 filters × 27 weights = 2592 parameters.

demo_steps.title: Spatial size is untouched
demo_steps.narration: Switch to spatial view: both slabs' faces stay 128×128. The convolution layer remaps channels while preserving spatial resolution.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique layout, all elements on one horizontal row centered at y=0; +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal (drawn up-and-right at ~40° on screen). INPUT SLAB: front-left face is a true square 4.0 (X-height? no) — precisely: face lies in the X–Y plane as 0-thickness? Use box X = depth(channels), Y = 4.0 (the 128 height), Z = 4.0 (the 128 width receding diagonal); the visible true rectangle is the left face (Y×Z projected) and the slab extends toward the viewer along X. Input box: X = 0.75 (3 channels), Y = 4.0, Z = 4.0, centered at (-5.2, 0, 0), subdivided into 3 equal sheets by 2 interior lines on the top and front faces. Output box: X = depth(K), Y = 4.0, Z = 4.0, centered at (+5.2, 0, 0), subdivided into visible sheets with two '...' gaps. Depth mapping (matches the source's compressed look): depth_world(K) = 0.75 + 1.15·log(K/3)/log(32), so K=3 → 0.75 and K=96 → 1.90. Draw at most ~14 sheet lines regardless of K; insert three-dot ellipses (upper receding face and front face) where sheets are omitted. FILTER BOX: rounded rectangle, width 4.4, height 1.9, corner radius 0.35, stroke weight ~0.07, white fill, centered at (0,0,0) facing the camera; text 'Filter Bank with' / '3x3 filters' in a serif face. ARROWS: hollow block arrows (5-sided outline, white fill, black stroke ~0.05), length 1.5, shaft height 0.55, head height 1.1, centered at (-2.7, -0.15, 0) and (+2.7, -0.15, 0), both pointing +X. LABELS: '3' at (-5.2, -2.7, 0) under input; '96' (or current K) at (+5.2, -2.7, 0) under output; '128' at input left vertical edge (-6.6, 0, 0) and along input upper receding edge (-5.0, +2.5, 1.0); '128' at output right vertical edge (+7.6, +0.6, 0) and along output lower receding edge (+7.0, -2.0, -0.5). Headers: 'x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}' at (-5.2, 3.6, 0), 'x_out ∈ R^{96×128×128}' at (+5.2, 3.6, 0) with the 96 updating with the slider. PALETTE: pure line-art — white fills #FFFFFF, black strokes #000000, black text; highlight color for the selected filter and its linked channels warm orange #E8710A at ~35% fill opacity; secondary spatial-view highlight steel blue #2C6FBB at ~25% fill on the 128×128 faces. Selected-filter overlay: 3×3×3 grid of small cubes, cube side 0.2 with 0.04 gaps, drawn just in front of / above the filter box at (0, 1.6, 0.6), three slices separated along the receding axis, each slice color-matched to the input channel sheet it multiplies.
interactionPlan.notes: Build slabs as a single BoxGeometry per tensor plus separate thin plane strips for the sheet divider lines; render all edges with LineSegments (EdgesGeometry) at constant screen-space width using a fat-line material so the figure keeps its pen-and-ink look. Use an OrthographicCamera with a shear applied to the projection matrix (or simply place the camera so the left face projects as a true rectangle) for the oblique pose. Labels and headers as CSS2DRenderer/HTML overlays so LaTeX-style math (x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}) renders crisply with KaTeX and can update live with the slider. Hollow block arrows: ExtrudeGeometry of a 7-point arrow Shape with a white front face and black outline drawn from the shape's path. Rounded rect box: RoundedBoxGeometry or a Shape with quadratic corners, flat-facing camera. When filterCount changes, rebuild only the output slab's divider lines and rescale the box along X (animate over ~250 ms) — keep Y and Z fixed so the preserved 128×128 face is visually obvious. Ellipsis dots are small sphere/circle sprites always billboarded to the camera. Click picking via Raycaster against invisible per-filter proxy planes tiled across the filter box face; on select, set emissive/overlay material on the corresponding input sheets and the one output sheet, and fade all other geometry to 25% opacity. Orbit limited to ±25° azimuth and ±20° elevation around the oblique pose so the figure never loses its diagram-like read.

authoredContext:
It's important to get comfortable with the shapes of the data and
parameter tensors that get processed through different neural
architectures. This is essential when designing and building these
architectures, and when analyzing and debugging them. Let's go through
an example with concrete numbers. Consider data
$\mathbf{x}_{\texttt{in}}$, which is an RGB image of size
$128 \times 128$ pixels. We will pass it through a convoluational layer
that applies a bank of $3 \times 3$ filters (this refers to the spatial
extent of the filters). We omit the bias terms for simplicity. The
output ends up being a $96 \times 128 \times 128$ tensor, as shown in
the figure.

A convolutional layer that applies a bank of $3 \times 3$ filters. How many parameters does each filter have? How many filters are in the filter bank? Source: created by Jonas Wulff.

discrepancies: The two block arrows (input → filter bank → output) are absent from the render; their stroke meshes appear to be back-face culled (clockwise winding with default FrontSide material), so the flow of the diagram is lost.
The rounded-rectangle outline around 'Filter Bank with 3x3 filters' does not appear — only the bare text floats in the middle, whereas the source shows a prominent thick-stroked rounded box.
Colour scheme differs: the source is pure black-on-white line art, while both slabs are filled with a translucent orange 'channel emphasis' wash by default, changing the figure's overall look.

The ellipsis marks are much less legible than in the source: the output slab shows one faint '...' on the front face and a barely visible cluster on the top, while the source has clear '…' in two distinct gap regions.
Output slab thickness is compressed relative to the source — in the original the 96-channel slab is visibly much thicker than the 3-channel slab (roughly 2–3×); here the difference is modest.
evaluation.notes: Slab geometry, oblique projection and labelling closely follow the source and the interaction set (filter-count slider, emphasis toggle, filter selection, stepped demo) is rich and conceptually apt, but the two block arrows and the filter-bank rounded box fail to render and the default orange wash departs from the source's clean line-art look.
action_items: Set side: THREE.DoubleSide (or fix polygon winding) on strokeMat/fillMat so the block arrows and the rounded 'Filter Bank' box actually render as in the source.
Default the emphasis to 'none' (white slabs with black edges) so the initial view matches the source's line art, and make Channel/Spatial washes opt-in.
Increase the size/contrast of the ellipsis dots and place them in the two skipped-divider gaps so they read as '…' like the original.

Increase the visual thickness ratio between the 3-channel and 96-channel slabs so the channel-count growth reads at a glance, and bump label font sizes slightly for the 128/3/96 dimension annotations.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual plan and interaction set are sound (concept 5, no plan action items); the failures are implementation-level rendering bugs like back-face culling, default color wash, ellipsis legibility, and slab proportions.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique layout, all elements on one horizontal row centered at y=0; +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal (drawn up-and-right at ~40° on screen). INPUT SLAB: front-left face is a true square 4.0 (X-height? no) — precisely: face lies in the X–Y plane as 0-thickness? Use box X = depth(channels), Y = 4.0 (the 128 height), Z = 4.0 (the 128 width receding diagonal); the visible true rectangle is the left face (Y×Z projected) and the slab extends toward the viewer along X. Input box: X = 0.75 (3 channels), Y = 4.0, Z = 4.0, centered at (-5.2, 0, 0), subdivided into 3 equal sheets by 2 interior lines on the top and front faces. Output box: X = depth(K), Y = 4.0, Z = 4.0, centered at (+5.2, 0, 0), subdivided into visible sheets with two '...' gaps. interactionPlan.notes: Build slabs as a single BoxGeometry per tensor plus separate thin plane strips for the sheet divider lines; render all edges with LineSegments (EdgesGeometry) at constant screen-space width using a fat-line material so the figure keeps its pen-and-ink look. Use an OrthographicCamera with a shear applied to the projection matrix (or simply place the camera so the left face projects as a true rectangle) for the oblique pose. Labels and headers as CSS2DRenderer/HTML overlays so LaTeX-style math (x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}) renders crisply with KaTeX and can update live with the slider. Hollow block arrows: ExtrudeGeometry of a 7-point arrow Shape with a white front face and black outline drawn from the shape's path. Rounded rect box: RoundedBoxGeometry or a Shape with quadratic corners, flat-facing camera. When filterCount changes, rebuild only the output slab's divider lines and rescale the box along X (animate over ~250 ms) — keep Y and Z fixed so the preserved 128×128 face is visually obvious. Ellipsis dots are small sphere/circle sprites always billboarded to the camera. Click picking via Raycaster against invisible per-filter proxy planes tiled across the filter box face; on select, set emissive/overlay material on the corresponding input sheets and the one output sheet, and fade all other geometry to 25% opacity. Orbit limited to ±25° azimuth and ±20° elevation around the oblique pose so the figure never loses its diagram-like read.

discrepancies: The input slab in the source is drawn with 3 clearly separated channel sheets with visible gaps and a distinctly thin overall depth; the generated input slab shows 4-ish thin dividers crammed near the back edge rather than 3 evenly-spaced sheets across the slab thickness, so the '3 channels' reading is weaker.

Output slab ellipsis: the source shows two '...' marks (one on the top receding face, one on the front face) indicating skipped channels. The generated figure only shows one visible dot triplet on the front face; the top-face triplet appears squashed/rendered as a small blob near the top rather than a clean '...'.

Proportions: in the source, the output slab thickness is roughly 2–3× the input but the receding depth (128) is visibly large and equal on both slabs; in the generated version the output slab's depth face looks larger/deeper than the input's, giving an inconsistent 128×128 footprint between the two tensors.

Arrow shape: source block arrows are large, evenly-stroked outline arrows sitting clear of the filter-bank box; in the generated figure the arrow tails visually intersect/abut the rounded rectangle, and they are smaller relative to the box.

Label placement: the source places '128' at the top-left of the input slab along the receding top edge and '128' at the bottom-right of the output along the bottom depth edge; the generated '128' labels sit slightly off their edges (e.g. the right-side 128 floats away from the depth edge) making the dimension-to-edge mapping less obvious.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-composed recreation of the conv-layer tensor diagram with a correct oblique projection, all major labels, and a rich set of meaningful interactions (filter-count slider, emphasis modes, filter selection with kernel overlay, stepped demo); main weaknesses are the input slab's channel dividers not reading clearly as 3 sheets, an inconsistent depth footprint between input and output slabs, and a muddled top-face ellipsis.
action_items: Space the input slab's 2 interior dividers evenly across its thickness so the three 128×128 channel sheets are visually distinct, matching the source's gapped sheets.

Render the top-face '...' as three clearly separated coplanar dots (or a flat HTML label) so it reads as an ellipsis rather than a blob, and make sure both the top and front ellipses are visible as in the source.
Match the receding depth (128) of the input and output slabs exactly and position the '128' labels flush against the corresponding edges (top-left of input, right and bottom-right of output).
Enlarge the block arrows slightly and add clearance between arrow tails and the rounded Filter Bank rectangle so they don't overlap.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (no plan action items); all issues are concrete rendering fixes like divider spacing, ellipsis dots, matching slab depths, label placement, and arrow clearance.

interactions.teaches: One filter spans ALL input channels: clicking a filter in the bank lights up its 3 kernel slices (27 weights = 3×3×3), all three input channel sheets it reads from, and the single output sheet it writes to — so each filter costs 3·3·3 = 27 parameters and produces exactly one output channel.
